key_insight: Micropillar compression reveals that in anorthite, mechanical twinning is the easiest deformation mode (~300 MPa CRSS) while slip strength depends strongly on temperature, especially for specific slip systems.
engineering_relevance: These quantified deformation thresholds improve constitutive modeling of plagioclase-rich crustal rocks, helping predict when brittle vs. plastic behavior will control crustal rheology.
method: Focused-ion-beam milled ~1 µm micropillars from three crystal orientations
Compressed 36 pillars inside an SEM at 25, 300, or 800 °C
Measured yield stress and inferred CRSS for twinning and slip systems
evidence_signal: The study uses uniaxial SEM micropillar tests on 36 anorthite pillars to compare temperature-dependent yield behavior and resolve activation of twinning versus distinct slip systems.
watch_item: Micropillar results probe small, oriented volumes and may not fully capture scaling, defects, or interaction effects present in natural polycrystalline crustal rocks.
paper_title: Quantification of plastic deformation in anorthite using micropillar compression
